entries.fact: ocfs2_dinode is explicitly documented as an on-disk inode; i_flags is a direct __le32 member. This establishes the local source representation contract, not measured runtime bytes or an independently reviewed external specification.

The primary mask macros are ordinary integer constants: SUPER_BLOCK=0x20, LOCAL_ALLOC=0x40, CHAIN=0x400, DEALLOC=0x800; their OR is 0x00000c60. The analyzer only labels a bitmask pattern; it does not expand these macros or compute this value.

This supports a conditional source mismatch when the big-endian implementation applies; no preprocessing/build execution was performed.

entries.fact: The parent primary directly masks the raw on-disk word with host constants; the fix converts that read with le32_to_cpu before applying exactly the same mask. Each reviewed condition contains one i_flags access, so this primary does not exercise the analyzer's repeated-text binding limitation.

The only direct call found in same-revision fs/ocfs2 is in ocfs2_filecheck_repair_inode_block. A true return permits interpreting id2 as an extent list and potentially changing l_next_free_rec; changed metadata causes checksum recomputation and a dirty buffer. This is a source-level potential consequence, not observed corruption.

Repair returns immediately when its validation succeeds. Reaching the primary requires that validation fail, filesystem not be hard/soft read-only, buffer not be journal-owned, signature be valid, and VALID_FL remain set. i_blkno/fs_generation may be repaired before the primary. The special flags are not converted or rewritten before this read.

The repair callback casts bh->b_data to struct ocfs2_dinode. The filecheck read helper supplies that callback to ocfs2_read_blocks when type is nonzero. ocfs2_read_blocks allocates/obtains a buffer at the inode block number, submits READ when appropriate, waits for success, then calls validate(sb,bh) only when the buffer needs validation. It may use cached data or skip journal/dirty buffers, so disk I/O is a conditional source path.

evidence.excerpt:
static int
ocfs2_filecheck_read_inode_block_full(struct inode *inode,
				      struct buffer_head **bh,
				      int flags, int type)
{
	int rc;
	struct buffer_head *tmp = *bh;

	if (!type) /* Check inode block */
		rc = ocfs2_read_blocks(INODE_CACHE(inode),
				OCFS2_I(inode)->ip_blkno,
				1, &tmp, flags,
				ocfs2_filecheck_validate_inode_block);
	else /* Repair inode block */
		rc = ocfs2_read_blocks(INODE_CACHE(inode),
				OCFS2_I(inode)->ip_blkno,
				1, &tmp, flags,
				ocfs2_filecheck_repair_inode_block);

entries.fact: The filecheck fix sysfs operation passes FILECHECK_FIX to ocfs2_iget; only an I_NEW inode invokes ocfs2_read_locked_inode. Its can_lock branch uses the filecheck helper with type=1 and IGNORE_CACHE, and its alternate sync-read branch invokes repair when FILECHECK_FIX is set and the buffer is not journal-owned. A cached inode can bypass this chain.
